title: Orphaned privilege detection and proof bundling — prototype notes
content:
Background:

We regularly run quarterly privileged-access recertification, but gaps remain: stale service accounts, forgotten role grants, long-lived keys attached to deprecated roles, and delegated owners who have left teams. Current process relies on manual spreadsheets and ad-hoc evidence collection (screenshots, email threads). This doc captures a prototype approach for automating detection of 'orphaned' privileges and producing a bundled, verifiable evidence packet suitable for auditors and SIEM ingestion. Focus is RBAC v2 role graph snapshots, audit log alignment, and deterministic proof packaging for quarterly recert cycles.

Goals:
- Detect likely-orphaned principals (users, service accounts, keys) with high precision and low noise.
- Produce an immutable evidence bundle per detected item that includes role-graph snapshot, last-use events, attestation window, and owner-delegation chain.
- Export evidence metadata to SIEM (ECS-compatible) and to the recert platform.
- Provide a human-friendly review UI + one-click remediation (deactivate, rotate, reassign owner).

Scope & non-goals:
- Scope: AWS/GCP IAM, Kubernetes serviceaccounts, Vault tokens, platform-level RBAC v2 roles (console/API).
- Non-goal: full org-wide entitlement-proofing in MVP; we target high-risk sets (privileged admin roles, external service keys, long-lived tokens).

Heuristics for orphan detection (prototype):
1) Last-used latency: principal last-auth timestamp > 180 days and no scheduled automation or cron.
2) Role-change orphaning: role grants exist but the grantor/owner is offboarded (no active SSO mapping).
3) Key mismatch: active API keys with no corresponding recent API calls (token age > 90d + no inbound traffic).
4) Sparse trace footprint: principal appears only in infra provisioning logs but not in runtime traces for >120d.
5) Shadowed service account: SA bound to ephemeral pods that no longer exist (k8s deployment removed).

Each heuristic gets a confidence score, then composite score determines triage bucket (auto-suggest revoke, request attestation, or skip).

Required evidence items per finding (proof bundle format):
- id: deterministic UUID (sha256 of role-graph-timestamp + principal-id)
- produced_at: ISO timestamp
- principal: {id, type, display_name}  <-- stored flat in metadata list
- role_snapshot: flat reference to snapshot file name (role-graph-YYYYMMDD.json)
- last_activity_events: list of up to 10 log lines (flattened strings)
- owner_chain: ordered list of owner principals (display names) and contact emails
- attestation_request: generated template sent to owner (subject + body) as saved text
- siem_export_ref: kafka topic + partition + offset (string)
- remediation_recommendation: revoke|rotate|reassign|noop
- evidence_hash: sha256 over canonical bundle (for auditor verification)

Note: the JSON stored in our artifact bucket will be the canonical bundle; we also push a small metadata row into the recert DB for fast UI listing.

Audit log schema mapping (prototype):
We will adopt an Elastic Common Schema (ECS)-inspired mapping to simplify SIEM rules and correlation. Example mapping notes (flat fields used in export):
- event_time: ISO timestamp
- event_actor_id: principal id (user|sa|key)
- event_actor_type: user|service_account|key|token
- event_action: grant|revoke|assume_role|token_create|token_use
- event_target_role: role-id
- event_request_id: trace id
- event_source_ip: ip
- event_resource_path: resource identifier (k8s/iam/console)
- event_metadata: short freeform string (flattened)

Sample SIEM export line (stringified for bundle):
2025-11-04T17:42:05Z | actor=svc-deploy-42 | type=service_account | action=token_use | role=infra-admin | resource=k8s/cluster-1/namespaces/ci | trace=abc123 | src=10.2.3.4

SIEM export architecture (prototype):
- Detectors run in infra namespace (k8s) and in serverless lambdas (cloud).
- Findings posted to a Kafka topic: security.orphaned-privileges.v1
- Consumer A: produces canonical evidence bundle to S3 (s3://redwood-evidence/orphaned/…)
- Consumer B: transforms items to ECS-flat events and emits to SIEM ingestion pipeline (Logstash/Fluentd)
- We tag exported SIEM events with evidence_hash so that SIEM alerts can reference the canonical bundle.

RBAC v2 role-graph snapshotting approach:
- Weekly snapshot of role graph across systems. Snapshot normalized to CSV rows: role_id, member_id, grantor_id, grant_ts, inheritance_path.
- Store both normalized CSV for query and a compressed canonical JSON for proofs. Snapshot naming convention: role-graph-<system>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json.gz
- Snapshots are signed with a CI key and have a manifest (manifest.csv) that lists hash + signer.

Automation flow (end-to-end):
1) Ingest: collectors (iam scanner + k8s watcher + vault scavenger) append raw events to topic raw.security.identity.v1
2) Detector workers consume raw topic and apply heuristics -> emit findings to security.orphaned-privileges.v1
3) Evidence bundler consumes findings -> constructs canonical bundle, signs it, writes bundle to S3 and metadata row to recert DB
4) SIEM bridge consumes same bundle metadata -> emits ECS events with link to S3 bundle and evidence_hash
5) UI/runner polls recert DB and surfaces one-click actions that call remediation API (revoke/rotate)

Remediation safety: all auto-revoke actions are gated behind two conditions: confidence >= 0.9 AND no active dependents discovered via call-graph analysis. Otherwise we create attestation request to owner with 7-day SLA.

Rollout plan (quarterly milestones):
- Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks): run detectors in read-only mode, generate bundles but do not notify owners. Triage high-confidence findings with SRE/security.
- Phase 1 (next 6 weeks): enable SIEM export + owner attestation emails for high-risk items. Manual remediation via UI only.
- Phase 2 (quarterly): enable automated deactivation for bucket A (privileged, clearly orphaned) under guardrail flags.

QA, metrics and dashboards to build:
- False positive rate (FP/total flagged) — target < 10% for auto-suggest cluster.
- Time-to-attestation median (owner response) — target < 7 days.
- Bundles produced per week + size distribution.
- SIEM alerts generated from bundles + investigation outcomes.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Ownership model for service accounts that are team-owned vs infra-owned -> need SRE+platform agreement.
- How to treat service principals used by third-party integrations (external vendor tokens). Policy: escalate to vendor-security review.
- Signing key lifecycle for bundle manifests — HSM or KMS? Recommend KMS with rotation and reproducible signer identity.
- Snapshots retention policy and encryption: default 3 years encrypted at rest.

Immediate action items (owners & ETA):
- Build detector prototype (Marco) — 2026-01-24
- Role-graph snapshot job (Priya) — 2026-01-17
- SIEM mapping doc and Logstash pipeline stub (Liam) — 2026-01-31
- Draft owner attestation email templates (Aisha) — 2025-11-15 (done, saved in linked artifacts)

Notes / scratch:
- Consider adding a "stewardship tag" on roles that are intentionally long-lived (e.g., platform-bastion) so we don't repeatedly flag them.
- For Kubernetes, combine RBAC v2 binding scans with pod lifecycle to detect true orphaned SAs.
- Proof-bundles should be immutable and easily referenced by auditors; include a small human-readable summary (1–2 lines) for each item for quick review.

Next check-in: security sync on 2026-01-12 — demo prototype outputs and a handful of curated bundles for the pilot team.

Appendix A — quick SIEM queries (example Kibana DSL simplified into text):
- Find unused keys: event_action:token_use AND event_actor_type:key AND last_seen:<now-90d => returns candidates
- Owners without response: tag:attestation_pending AND attestation_sent_at:<now-7d AND attestation_response:null

Appendix B — example canonical bundle filename:
- orphaned-20260105-<sha1>.json.gz (contains canonical fields + base64-encoded sign block)

End of prototype notes.
